// Package bindadapter adapts streams and event sources to wasmbind hooks.
// Interruption callbacks must be safe alongside an active operation and must
// unblock it. Cancellation permanently interrupts that direction. Events use
// the caller's channel or an explicitly bounded blocking queue; no events drop.
package bindadapter

import (
 "context"
 "errors"
 "io"
 "iter"
 "sync"
 "sync/atomic"
)

// ErrBusy reports overlapping operations on one adapter direction.
var ErrBusy = errors.New("adapter operation already pending")
// ErrClosed reports an operation after interruption or completion.
var ErrClosed = errors.New("adapter is closed")

type interruption struct { once sync.Once; stopped atomic.Bool; fn func()error; err error }
func (i *interruption) interrupt()error {
 i.once.Do(func(){ i.stopped.Store(true);i.err=callInterrupt(i.fn) })
 return i.err
}
func callInterrupt(fn func()error)(err error) {
 defer func(){if recover()!=nil{err=errors.New("adapter interruption panicked")}}()
 return fn()
}
// duringCancel waits for a cancellation hook that has already started. This
// prevents a late hook from interrupting the next operation on the direction.
func duringCancel(ctx context.Context, interrupt func()error)func() {
 done:=make(chan struct{})
 stop:=context.AfterFunc(ctx,func(){defer close(done);_ = interrupt()})
 return func(){if !stop(){<-done}}
}

// Reader serializes a context-aware byte source. Its zero value is not usable.
type Reader struct { stop interruption; busy atomic.Bool; read func(context.Context,[]byte)(int,error) }
// NewReader constructs a reader with an explicit interruption contract.
func NewReader(read func(context.Context,[]byte)(int,error), interrupt func()error)(*Reader,error) {
 if read==nil || interrupt==nil {return nil,errors.New("reader requires read and interrupt callbacks")}
 return &Reader{read:read,stop:interruption{fn:interrupt}},nil
}
// ReadCloser adapts an io.ReadCloser; cancellation closes the source.
func ReadCloser(r io.ReadCloser)(*Reader,error) {
 if r==nil{return nil,errors.New("reader is nil")}
 return NewReader(func(_ context.Context,p []byte)(int,error){return r.Read(p)},r.Close)
}
// Read reads one chunk. One Read may run at a time.
func (r *Reader) Read(ctx context.Context,p []byte)(int,error) {
 if err:=ctx.Err();err!=nil{return 0,err}
 if r.stop.stopped.Load(){return 0,ErrClosed}
 if !r.busy.CompareAndSwap(false,true){return 0,ErrBusy};defer r.busy.Store(false)
 stop:=duringCancel(ctx,r.Interrupt);defer stop()
 n,err:=r.read(ctx,p);if n<0 || n>len(p){return 0,errors.New("invalid read count")}
 if err==nil && ctx.Err()!=nil{err=ctx.Err()};return n,err
}
// Interrupt unblocks the read and permanently closes its direction.
func (r *Reader) Interrupt()error{return r.stop.interrupt()}
// Close interrupts the source. Resource disposal waits for active bridge leases.
func (r *Reader) Close()error{return r.Interrupt()}

// Writer serializes writing and finishing. Its zero value is not usable.
type Writer struct {stop interruption;busy atomic.Bool;finished atomic.Bool;write func(context.Context,[]byte)(int,error);finish func(context.Context)error}
// NewWriter constructs a writer with separate finish and interruption hooks.
func NewWriter(write func(context.Context,[]byte)(int,error), finish func(context.Context)error, interrupt func()error)(*Writer,error) {
 if write==nil || finish==nil || interrupt==nil{return nil,errors.New("writer requires write, finish and interrupt callbacks")}
 return &Writer{write:write,finish:finish,stop:interruption{fn:interrupt}},nil
}
// WriteCloser adapts an io.WriteCloser; finishing or interruption closes it once.
func WriteCloser(w io.WriteCloser)(*Writer,error) {
 if w==nil{return nil,errors.New("writer is nil")}
 var once sync.Once;var err error
 close:=func()error{once.Do(func(){err=w.Close()});return err}
 return NewWriter(func(_ context.Context,p []byte)(int,error){return w.Write(p)},func(context.Context)error{return close()},close)
}
// Write writes one chunk. It does not retry partial writes; the bridge does.
func(w *Writer) Write(ctx context.Context,p []byte)(int,error) {
 if err:=ctx.Err();err!=nil{return 0,err}
 if w.stop.stopped.Load() || w.finished.Load(){return 0,ErrClosed}
 if !w.busy.CompareAndSwap(false,true){return 0,ErrBusy};defer w.busy.Store(false)
 stop:=duringCancel(ctx,w.Interrupt);defer stop()
 n,err:=w.write(ctx,p);if n<0 || n>len(p){return 0,errors.New("invalid write count")}
 if err==nil && ctx.Err()!=nil{err=ctx.Err()};return n,err
}
// Finish completes writing. One write or finish may run at a time.
func(w *Writer) Finish(ctx context.Context)error {
 if err:=ctx.Err();err!=nil{return err}
 if w.finished.Load(){return nil};if w.stop.stopped.Load(){return ErrClosed}
 if !w.busy.CompareAndSwap(false,true){return ErrBusy};defer w.busy.Store(false)
 stop:=duringCancel(ctx,w.Interrupt);defer stop()
 err:=w.finish(ctx);if err==nil{w.finished.Store(true);if ctx.Err()!=nil{err=ctx.Err()}};return err
}
// Interrupt unblocks writing and permanently closes its direction.
func(w *Writer) Interrupt()error{return w.stop.interrupt()}
// Close releases writing without calling Finish.
func(w *Writer) Close()error{if w.finished.Load(){return nil};return w.Interrupt()}

// Events serializes pulls from an event source. Its zero value is not usable.
type Events[T any] struct {stop interruption;busy atomic.Bool;finished atomic.Bool;next func(context.Context)(T,bool,error);done <-chan struct{}}
// NewEvents constructs a pull source without adding a queue. The interruption
// callback must unblock Next. A false result or error permanently ends iteration.
func NewEvents[T any](next func(context.Context)(T,bool,error), interrupt func()error)(*Events[T],error) {
 if next==nil || interrupt==nil{return nil,errors.New("events require next and interrupt callbacks")}
 return &Events[T]{next:next,stop:interruption{fn:interrupt}},nil
}
// Next pulls one value. One Next may run at a time.
func(e *Events[T]) Next(ctx context.Context)(T,bool,error) {
 var zero T
 if err:=ctx.Err();err!=nil{return zero,false,err}
 if e.finished.Load() || e.stop.stopped.Load(){return zero,false,nil}
 if !e.busy.CompareAndSwap(false,true){return zero,false,ErrBusy};defer e.busy.Store(false)
 stop:=duringCancel(ctx,e.Interrupt);defer stop()
 v,more,err:=e.next(ctx);if err==nil && ctx.Err()!=nil{err=ctx.Err()}
 if !more || err!=nil{e.finished.Store(true)};return v,more,err
}
// Interrupt stops further pulls and unblocks an active pull.
func(e *Events[T]) Interrupt()error{return e.stop.interrupt()}
// Close interrupts iteration and waits for a generated sequence producer.
func(e *Events[T]) Close()error {err:=e.Interrupt();if e.done!=nil{<-e.done};return err}
// FromChannel receives values from the supplied channel without an extra queue.
// The optional interrupt callback releases the source's own producer resources.
func FromChannel[T any](source <-chan T, interrupt func()error)(*Events[T],error) {
 if source==nil{return nil,errors.New("event channel is nil")}
 done:=make(chan struct{})
 return NewEvents(func(ctx context.Context)(T,bool,error){var zero T;select{case <-ctx.Done():return zero,false,ctx.Err();case <-done:return zero,false,nil;case v,ok:=<-source:return v,ok,nil}},func()error{close(done);if interrupt!=nil{return interrupt()};return nil})
}
// FromSeq2 runs a sequence through a blocking queue of exactly capacity values.
// Capacity zero uses rendezvous. Interrupt must unblock the sequence producer;
// Close waits for it. Values are not copied: producers must not mutate values
// after yielding. An error ends the sequence and is delivered once.
func FromSeq2[T any](source iter.Seq2[T,error], interrupt func()error, capacity int)(*Events[T],error) {
 if source==nil || interrupt==nil || capacity<0{return nil,errors.New("sequence requires source, interrupt and nonnegative capacity")}

 e.done=done

 return e,nil
}
// FromSeq adapts a value sequence with the same bounded queue contract as FromSeq2.
func FromSeq[T any](source iter.Seq[T], interrupt func()error, capacity int)(*Events[T],error) {
 if source==nil{return nil,errors.New("sequence is nil")}
